exec: The UK's offensive cyber unit now has a permanent base, tied to a regional cyber skills and jobs push in the North West.
plain: King Charles formally opened Ribble House, the new headquarters of the National Cyber Force, the UK's unit for offensive cyber operations, in Samlesbury, Lancashire.

key_findings: King Charles III officially opened Ribble House, the National Cyber Force headquarters in Samlesbury, Lancashire.
The NCF is a defence and intelligence partnership of GCHQ and the Ministry of Defence, also drawing on Dstl and MI6.
It runs cyber operations to support the military, counter state threats and disrupt criminals and terrorists, and does not routinely publish operational details.
The release cites a Digital and Cyber Bursary supporting 500 local college students but gives no investment or staffing figures.
recommendations: The release contains no guidance for organisations.

summary: The UK government announced that King Charles III officially opened Ribble House, the National Cyber Force's new headquarters in Samlesbury, Lancashire. The NCF is a GCHQ and Ministry of Defence partnership, drawing on Dstl and MI6, that runs cyber operations to support the military, counter state threats and disrupt criminals and terrorists. The release gives no cost or staffing figures; press coverage cites a GBP 5 billion commitment through 2030.
title: King Charles opens new headquarters for the UK's National Cyber Force
